subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, including already-persisted omitted jobs, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` remain an invalid one-shot-only contract?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite cron lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects upgrade behavior, session retention, and user recovery for existing scheduled jobs.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add upgrade/load or doctor handling for existing omitted isolated recurring jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Choose the strict one-shot-only contract and pause or close this PR after documenting recovery for existing invalid jobs.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land only the new create default while explicitly documenting that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add upgrade/load or doctor handling for existing omitted isolated recurring jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron normalization, SQLite persisted-state behavior, and product compatibility, and steipete has recent history across those paths.
